 ORDER
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, matter is heard finally at motion stage.

2. This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellant under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by award dated 27.09.2018 passed by 5th Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Junnardeo District Chhindwara (M.P.) in MACC No.14/2015 seeking reduction of compensation as well as exoneration from liability to pay compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Junnardeo District Chhindwara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the appellant after referring to para 17 of impugned award as well as evidence on record submits that tribunal has wrongly added Rs.1000/- to deceased's monthly income.
It is also urged that deceased was bachelor at the time of accident, Therefore, one half should have been deducted for personal and living expenses.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that at the time of accident offending vehicle was being used as taxi and therefore, plied in breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy.
It is also urged that even if fare was not paid by passenger traveling in the offending vehicle, still they would be considered as gratuitous passenger.
It is also urged that tribunal wrongly awarded consortium to respondents No.2 to 4 are brother/sister of deceased.
It is also urged that interest awarded by tribunal be reduced by 3%.
On above grounds, it is urged that compensation awarded by tribunal be reduced appellant/insurance company be exonerated from liability to pay the compensation.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent submitted that impugned award passed by the tribunal is just and proper and no interference is required in the same.
Hence appeal filed by the appellant be dismissed.
5 I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.

6. So far as income of deceased is concerned, perusal of para 17 of impugned award reveals that admittedly at the time of accident, deceased was working as Village Panchayat Secretary and thereby The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Shri Dulichand on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4393831/
2 earning Rs.5000/- per month.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited vs Shri Dulichand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Tribunal has also held that deceased was also assisting in agricultural etc.
In this Court's considered opinion, respondents/claimants have not filed any documents to show that deceased was having any agricultural land in his name.
Therefore, tribunal has wrongly added Rs.1000/- to the income of deceased.
Thus deceased's income is determined as Rs.5000/- per month.
7. Further, deceased was bachelor at the time of accident.

Therefore, in view of law laid down of Smt.
Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. , AIR 2009 SC 3104, one half should have been deducted for personal and living expenses and tribunal has wrongly deducted 1/3.
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of above annual income of deceased comes to Rs.90,000/-
(Rs.5000/- x 12 50%).

After deducting  for personal and living expenses, annual dependency comes to Rs.45,000/-.
8.
In the instant case, multiplier of 17 is to be applied and thus total loss of dependency comes to Rs.7,65,000/-.
9. Perusal of impugned award reveal that tribunal awarded consortium to each of applicants.
In the instant case, appellants No.2,3,4 are brother/sister of deceased.
Therefore, they are not entitled to receive consortium.

10. In view of above, total compensation come to Rs.8,35,000/-(Rs.7,65,000 70,000).
11.

So far as breach of terms and condition aforesaid insurance policy is concerned, perusal of paras 10 and 13 of impugned award reveal that tribunal has rightly held that from evidence on record, it is not proved that offending vehicle was being plied in breach of terms and condition of insurance policy.
Further, no reduction in rate of interest is required in the facts and circumstances of the case.
12. In view of above, appeal filed by the appellant is partly allowed and compensation awarded by tribunal i.e Rs.14,14,000/- is reduced to Rs.8,35,000/-.
14. Respondents/claimants are entitled to receive Rs.8,35,000/- as compensation.
Other remaining findings of Tribunal shall remain intact.
15. Accordingly, appeal filed by the appellant is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
